hallucinations.claim: a nightly rate of $90–$150 may serve as a reasonable starting point
hallucinations.why: Benchmarked against weekend hotel rates, not monthly apartment comps. For a 30+ night stay that works out to ~$2,700-4,500 a month (~R$15-25k), several times the reference R$5,000-8,000 furnished monthly range for a 2-bedroom.
Monthly stays are typically priced 25-40% below 30 x nightly. A 10-15% discount on a hotel-derived nightly rate overprices the listing badly.

hallucinations.why: Attributed to search snippets but irrelevant as a pricing basis for a monthly apartment rental. These are hotel-aggregator figures presented as the benchmark.

what_went_wrong: Search returned hotel and hostel aggregator pages, not monthly-rental comps. The gpt-oss draft anchored pricing on hotel weekend rates, and the review/verify pass only tidied citations instead of questioning the method. hallucinations.claim: (e.g., a 7 B model on an 8 GB GPU) | 8× memory savings
hallucinations.why: Models are distributed in bf16/fp16, so 4-bit is a 4x saving (7B: ~14 GB to ~4-5 GB), not 8x. The 8x figure assumes FP32 weights nobody ships.

hallucinations.claim: gradient checkpointing can break with 4-bit, so either avoid it or use float-32 checkpoints
hallucinations.why: Invented. QLoRA routinely runs with gradient checkpointing enabled; the paper and the bitsandbytes/PEFT recipes use it.

hallucinations.claim: QLoRA ... Requires a quantization-aware training pipeline
hallucinations.why: Wrong. QLoRA freezes NF4 base weights and trains LoRA adapters; it is not quantization-aware training.

hallucinations.claim: compresses every 32-bit weight ... min and max are per-layer calibration values
hallucinations.why: Stale or wrong: modern LLM weights are 16-bit, and practical 4-bit schemes (GPTQ, AWQ, GGUF Q4_K, MLX group-64) use per-group scales over 32-128 weights, not per-layer min/max.

hallucinations.claim: the impact on perplexity is usually below 1 % ... typical accuracy loss is 2–4 % on generation benchmarks
hallucinations.why: Specific figures with no source, and inconsistent with each other. They are presented as fact.

hallucinations.claim: int4 dot-products ... quantized queries and keys
hallucinations.why: Misleading: mainstream 4-bit inference is weight-only. Q/K activations stay 16-bit, so attention logits are not computed from int4 queries and keys.

what_went_wrong: The gpt-oss:20b draft came from model knowledge with no search and carried the FP32 baseline and per-layer mapping. The merge then ballooned it into a 2.9k-char answer with a table and invented fine-tuning caveats, ignoring 'keep it short'. The ministral review pushed for more content (attention, dynamic range) rather than correctness.
great_answer_would: In 4-6 sentences: 16-bit weights stored as 4-bit with per-group scales (7B ~14 GB to ~4-5 GB); decoding is bandwidth-bound, so it is ~2-3x faster; small quality cost at 7B+ that grows for tiny models, math/code and sub-4-bit; a bigger 4-bit model beats a smaller 16-bit one, and use 8-bit when memory allows.
notes: Leaves out the key 'why it matters' points: memory-bandwidth-bound decoding and the bigger-model-at-4-bit rule. Never mentions modern formats (AWQ, GPTQ, GGUF Q4_K_M, MLX, MXFP4 in gpt-oss), which Pat asked to have flagged. The outlier sensitivity point and the advice to stay at 8-bit when quality is critical are sound.
